excluded: any other Product Hunt rank or vote field
inputs.note: Website fields in the lineup were Product Hunt API redirect URLs, not product domains. X url: queries cannot include '/'; searches used product names, slugs, and listed maker/hunter handles. No Product Hunt pages were loaded. Each launch has two count rows (pre_launch: 48 hours ending 00:00 PT, and launch_day: 00:00 PT to 00:21 PT).

forecast.name: ByteAsk Cloud Agents
forecast.reason: By far the heaviest X conversation (149 pre-launch posts) about an AI coding agent that finds fixes in large/C++ codebases, including a 69,515-follower account in the sample and an Introducing thread with 54 visible reposts; no launch-morning posts yet.

forecast.name: Rakazo
forecast.reason: Clear product conversation over the prior 48 hours (44 posts), with a 70-like maker post and a 53,149-follower account amplifying an open-source Grok Bot alternative, plus one launch-morning reply offering to invest.

forecast.name: Tulvo
forecast.reason: The only launch with a sustained Product Hunt pre-announce: nine countdown posts from two small accounts (largest 127 followers) ahead of the 15 November debut. Reach is modest, but the intent signal is explicit.

forecast.name: Remindly
forecast.reason: No meaningful pre-launch buzz, but the maker posted an official Product Hunt launch announcement shortly after 00:00 PT (2 likes). That is the only launch-day announcement in the first 21 minutes.

forecast.name: Talyn
forecast.reason: No on-topic X posts in either window, but the lineup text is a sharp, timely hook -- run Claude Code and Codex in parallel cloud sandboxes -- so the ranking rests on that text, not observed buzz.

forecast.name: Perit Marketplace
forecast.reason: No on-topic X posts; ranked on lineup text alone -- a marketplace to sell data and RL tasks to frontier AI labs, which is a clear and unusual hook.

forecast.name: Polylane for Security
forecast.reason: No X posts found; the tagline (catch exploitable vulnerabilities before they ship) is a concrete, current-tooling hook that is easier to picture than the other silent, more generic tools.

forecast.name: Spiik
forecast.reason: No on-topic X posts; ranked on lineup text -- an AI note taker for meetings and lectures that does not put a bot on the call, a specific differentiator.

forecast.name: Pixel Office
forecast.reason: No on-topic X posts; the tagline (run a team of AI agents from a pixel-art office) is distinctive and memorable, which is why it sits above the remaining silent launches.

forecast.name: Canvas by AgentGrid.io
forecast.reason: No posts about the Canvas launch itself (only broader AgentGrid chatter, which was excluded). Ranked on the lineup text: an Agentic Design Canvas for visual collaboration with AI.
